source.snippet: Connections to my company's website using http rather than https are redirected [to] another site. Avast seems to block the site... After clicking, the user is directed to press Win Key+r and run the following command... — ServerFault, captured 2026-07-23. Score: -1 but describes a live attack scenario at a real company.

problem_statement: Small and mid-sized businesses suffer DNS hijack or HTTP-redirect injection attacks and lack the internal expertise to quickly detect, diagnose, and remediate the attack — often discovering it only via end-user reports or consumer AV software.
target_segment: IT administrators and small business owners at SMBs without a dedicated security team, running web-facing services.
notes: Real company affected by a live DNS hijack/HTTP-injection attack, discovered reactively. Buyer is the IT admin or business owner who would pay for proactive DNS and HTTP-redirect monitoring with alerting. Existing tools (Avast, etc.) detected but didn't prevent. Opportunity: a low-cost SaaS that continuously monitors a company's domain for unexpected HTTP/DNS redirects and alerts owners before customers are impacted. Single signal but business context is clear.
